nodes.name: Lemma 6: Centered moments deviations of Gaussian matrices
nodes.statement:
There is a constant $A_1>0$ such that for every pair of integers  $n\ge 8$ 
	and $p\ge 1$ and for every covariance matrix $\boldsymbol\Sigma$ such that 
	$\lambda_{\max}(\boldsymbol\Sigma) = 1$, we have
	align
		\mathbf E\Big[\|\boldsymbol\zeta_{1:n}\boldsymbol\zeta_{1:n}^\top-n\boldsymbol\Sigma\|_{\textup{op}}\Big] 
		&\le  A_1\big(\sqrt{n} 
			+ \sqrt{\textbf{\textup{r}}_{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol\Sigma}}\big)\sqrt{\textbf{\textup{r}}_{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol\Sigma}},\\
		\mathbf E\Big[\lambda_{\max,+}(\boldsymbol\zeta_{1:n}\boldsymbol\zeta_{1:n}^\top-n\boldsymbol\Sigma)\Big] 
		&\le  6\sqrt{np} + 4p,\\
		\mathbf E\Big[\lambda_{\max,+}(n\boldsymbol\Sigma - \boldsymbol\zeta_{1:n}\boldsymbol\zeta_{1:n}^\top)\Big] 
		&\le  6\sqrt{np},
	align	
	where the last inequality is valid under the additional assumption $p\le n$. 
	Furthermore, there is a constant $A_2>0$ such that 
	align
		\mathbf P\bigg(\|\boldsymbol\zeta_{1:n}\boldsymbol\zeta_{1:n}^\top-n\boldsymbol\Sigma\|_{\textup{op}} -
		\mathbf E\Big[\|\boldsymbol\zeta_{1:n}\boldsymbol\zeta_{1:n}^\top-n\boldsymbol\Sigma\|_{\textup{op}}\Big] 
		\ge A_2\Big(\sqrt{tn} + \sqrt{t\textbf{\textup{r}}_{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol\Sigma}}+t\Big)\bigg)\le e^{-t},\quad \forall t\ge 1.
	align

nodes.name: Lemma 4, Lemma 5: Moments deviations of singular values of Gaussian matrices
nodes.statement:
Let $\lambda_{\max}(\boldsymbol\Sigma)=1$. For every $t>0$ and for every 
	pair of positive integers $n$ and $p$, 
	we have
	align
		\mathbf E\big[s_{\max}(\boldsymbol\zeta_{1:n})\big] & \le \sqrt{n} + \sqrt{\textbf{\textup{r}}_{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol\Sigma}},\quad
		&\mathbf P\big(s_{\max}(\boldsymbol\zeta_{1:n})  \ge \sqrt{n} + \sqrt{\textbf{\textup{r}}_{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol\Sigma}} + 
		t\big)  \le e^{-t^2/2}.
	align
	If, in addition, $\boldsymbol\Sigma$ is the identity matrix, then
	align
		\mathbf E\big[s_{\min}(\boldsymbol\zeta_{1:n})\big] & \ge {\big(\sqrt{n}
		-\sqrt{p}\big)}_+,\quad
		&\mathbf P\big(s_{\min}(\boldsymbol\zeta_{1:n})  \le \sqrt{n} - \sqrt{p} 
		- t\big)  \le e^{-t^2/2}.
	align

For a subset $\bar J$ of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$, we denote by $\boldsymbol\zeta_{\bar J}$ the 
	$p\times |\bar J|$ matrix obtained by concatenating the vectors 
	$\{\boldsymbol\zeta_i: i\in\bar J\}$. Let the covariance matrix $\boldsymbol\Sigma$ be such that 
	$\lambda_{\max}(\boldsymbol\Sigma) =1$. For every pair of integers  $n,p\ge 1$ and for 
	every integer $m\in[1,n]$, we have
	align
		\mathbf E\big[s_{\max}^2(\boldsymbol\zeta_{1:n})\big] &\le  \big(\sqrt{\textbf{\textup{r}}_{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol\Sigma}} + 
		\sqrt{n}\big)^2 +4,\\
		\mathbf E\big[(s_{\max}(\boldsymbol\zeta_{1:n})^2-n)_+\big]			
			&\le 6\sqrt{n\textbf{\textup{r}}_{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol\Sigma}} + 4\textbf{\textup{r}}_{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol\Sigma},\qquad \forall n\ge 8,\\
		\mathbf E\big[(n-s_{\min}(\boldsymbol\xi_{1:n})^2)_+\big]			
			&\le 6\sqrt{np},\qquad \forall n\ge 8,\\
		\mathbf E\Big[\max_{|\bar J| = m} s_{\max}^2(\boldsymbol\zeta_{\bar J})\Big] &\le
				\big(\sqrt{\textbf{\textup{r}}_{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol\Sigma}} + \sqrt{m} +  1.81\sqrt{m \log(\nicefrac{ne}{m})}\big)^2
				+4.
	align

nodes.name: Lemma 1: Properties of the weights from the feasible set
nodes.statement:
For any integer $\ell>0$, let $\mathcal W_{n,\ell}$ be 
	the set of all $\boldsymbol w\in\boldsymbol\Delta^{n-1}$ such that $\max_i 
	w_i\le 1/\ell$. The following facts hold: 
	\vspace{-10pt}
	enumerate
		\item[\textup{   i)}] For every $J\subset \{1,\ldots,n\}$ such 
		that $|J|\ge \ell$, the uniform weight vector $\boldsymbol u^{J}\in 
		\mathcal W_{n,\ell}$.
		\item[\textup{  ii)}] The set $\mathcal W_{n,\ell}$ is 
		the convex hull of the uniform weight vectors $\{\boldsymbol u^{J} : 
		|J| = \ell\}$.
		\item[\textup{ iii)}] For every convex mapping 
		$G:\boldsymbol\Delta^{n-1}\to\mathbb R$,  we have 
		align
			\sup_{\boldsymbol w\in \mathcal W_{n,\ell}} G(\boldsymbol w) = 
			\max_{|J| =\ell} G(\boldsymbol u^J),
		align
		where the last maximum is over all subsets $J$ of cardinality 
		$\ell$ of the set $\{1,\ldots,n\}$.
		\item[\textup{ iv)}] If $\boldsymbol w\in\mathcal W_{n,\ell}$ then for any 
		$I$ such that $|I|\ge \ell'>n-\ell$, we have 
		$\boldsymbol w_{|I}\in \mathcal W_{n,\ell+\ell'-n}$.
	enumerate 
	\vspace{-10pt}

nodes.name: Lemma 7: Operator-norm error of weighted covariance of Gaussians
nodes.statement:
Let $p\ge 2$, $n\ge 4\vee p$, $m\in[2,0.6n]$ and $o\le m$ be four integers. 
	It holds that
	align
			\mathbf E&\Bigg[\sup_{\substack{\boldsymbol w\in \mathcal W_{n,n-m+o} \\ |I| \ge n-o}} 
			\lambda_{\max,+}\Big(\boldsymbol\Sigma - \sum_{i=1}^n (\boldsymbol w_{|I})_i\boldsymbol\zeta_i\boldsymbol\zeta_i^\top\Big
			)\Bigg] \le 25\sqrt{p/n} + 33(m/n) \log({n}/{m}).
			
			
			
	align
	Furthermore, for any $p\ge 1$, $n\ge 1$, $m\in[2,0.6n]$ and $o\le m$,
	align
			\mathbf E&\bigg[\sup_{\substack{\boldsymbol w\in \mathcal W_{n,n-m+o} \\ |I| \ge n-o}}  
			\Big\|\boldsymbol\Sigma - \sum_{i=1}^n (\boldsymbol w_{|I})_i\boldsymbol\zeta_i\boldsymbol\zeta_i^\top
			\Big\|_{\textup{op}}\bigg] \le (5.1A_1 + 2.5 A_2)\sqrt{\frac{\textbf{\textup{r}}_{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol\Sigma}}{n}} 
			+ 7.5A_2 \frac{m \log(\nicefrac{ne}{m})}{n},			
	align
	where $A_1$ and $A_2$ are the same constants as in 6.

nodes.name: Lemma 3: $\mathbb L_2$ -error of weighted averages of Gaussian vectors
nodes.statement:
Let $p\ge 1$, $n\ge 1$, $m\in[2,0.562n]$ and $o\in [0, m]$ be four positive integers. 
	It holds that
	align
			\mathbf E^{1/2}\Bigg[\sup_{\substack{\boldsymbol w\in \mathcal W_{n,n-m+o} \\ |I| \ge n-o}}
			{\|\bar{\boldsymbol\zeta}_{\boldsymbol w_{|I}}\|}_2^2\Bigg]  \le {\sqrt{\textbf{\textup{r}}_{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol\Sigma}/n}}\,
			\bigg(1+7\sqrt{\frac{m}{2n}}\bigg) + \frac{4.6m}{n}\sqrt{\log(\nicefrac{ne}{m})}.
	align

nodes.name: Proposition 1: Deterministic bound involving the weighted covariance
nodes.statement:
Let $\boldsymbol\zeta_1,\ldots,\boldsymbol\zeta_n$ be a set of vectors such 
	that $\boldsymbol\zeta_i = \boldsymbol X_i-\boldsymbol\mu^*$ for every $i\in \mathcal I$, 
	where $\mathcal I$ is a subset of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. For every 
	weight vector $\boldsymbol w\in \boldsymbol \Delta^{n-1}$ such that 
	$\sum_{i\not\in \mathcal I} w_i\le \varepsilon_{w}\le 1/2$ and 
	for every $p\times p$ matrix $\boldsymbol\Sigma$, it holds  
	align
	\|\bar{\boldsymbol X}_{\boldsymbol w} - {\boldsymbol\mu}^*\|_2 
		&\le \frac{\sqrt{\varepsilon_{w}}}{1-\varepsilon_{w}}\,
			\lambda_{\max,+}^{1/2}\Big(\sum_{i=1}^n  w_i(\boldsymbol X_i - 
			\bar{\boldsymbol X}_{\boldsymbol w})^{\otimes 2} 
			- \boldsymbol\Sigma\Big) + R(\boldsymbol\zeta,\boldsymbol w,\mathcal I),
	align
	with the remainder term
	align
	R(\boldsymbol\zeta,\boldsymbol w,\mathcal I) 
		= 2\sqrt{\|\boldsymbol\Sigma\|_{\rm op}}\varepsilon_{w}+\sqrt{2\varepsilon_{w}}\,
		\lambda_{\max,+}^{1/2}
		\bigg(\sum_{i\in \mathcal I} (\boldsymbol w_{|\mathcal I})_i (\boldsymbol\Sigma - 
		\boldsymbol\zeta_i\boldsymbol\zeta_i^\top)\bigg) + (1+\sqrt{2\varepsilon_{w}}) 
		\|\bar{\boldsymbol\zeta}_{\boldsymbol w_{|\mathcal I}}\|_2.
	align

nodes.name: Lemma 2: Assessing the Error of Initial Estimator geom median
nodes.statement:
For every $\varepsilon\le 1/2$, the geometric median satisfies the inequality
	align
		\|\widehat{\boldsymbol\mu}_n^{\textup{GM}} - \boldsymbol\mu^*\|_2 &\le 	
		\frac{2}{n(1-2\varepsilon)}\sum_{i=1}^n\|\boldsymbol\zeta_i\|_2.
	align
	Furthermore, its expected error satisfies
	align
		\|\widehat{\boldsymbol\mu}_n^{\textup{GM}} - \boldsymbol\mu^*\|_{\mathbb L_2} &\le 	
		 \frac{2\textbf{\textup{r}}_{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol\Sigma}^{1/2}}{1-2\varepsilon} .
	align

nodes.name: Proposition 2: Uniform bounds on the moments of Stochastic Terms
nodes.statement:
Let $R(\boldsymbol\zeta,\boldsymbol w, I)$ be defined in 1 and 
	$\boldsymbol\zeta_1,\ldots,\boldsymbol\zeta_n$ be i.i.d. centered Gaussian random 
	vectors with covariance matrix $\boldsymbol\Sigma$ satisfying 
	$\lambda_{\max}(\boldsymbol\Sigma) = 1$. If $\varepsilon\le 0.28$, 
	then the random variable 
	align
		\Xi = \sup_{\boldsymbol w\in \mathcal W_n(\varepsilon)} 
		\max_{|I|\ge n(1-\varepsilon)} R(\boldsymbol\zeta,\boldsymbol w, I)
	align
	satisfies, for a universal constant $C>0$, the inequalities 
	align
		\|\Xi\|_{\mathbb L_2} &\le \sqrt{\textbf{\textup{r}}_{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol\Sigma}/n}(1+ C
		\sqrt{\varepsilon}) + C\sqrt{\varepsilon}(\textbf{\textup{r}}_{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol\Sigma}/n)^{1/4} 
		+ C\varepsilon\sqrt{\log(1/\varepsilon)} \\
		\|\Xi\|_{\mathbb L_2} &\le \sqrt{p/n}(1+ 16\sqrt{\varepsilon})
		+ 5\sqrt{3\varepsilon}\,(p/n)^{1/4} + 
		32\varepsilon\sqrt{\log(2/\varepsilon)},
	align
	where for the second inequality we assumed that $p\ge 2$ and
	$n\ge p\vee 4$.

nodes.name: Theorem 1: Bound on Expected Error
nodes.statement:
Let $\widehat{\boldsymbol\mu}_n^{\textup{IR}}$ be the iteratively reweighted 
    mean defined in~6 and Algorithm~algo:a1. 
    There is a universal constant $C>0$ such that for any 
    $n,p\ge 1 $ and for every $\varepsilon < (5-\sqrt{5})/10$, 
    we have
    align
        \sup_{\boldsymbol\mu^*\in\mathbb R^p}
        \sup_{\mathbf P\!_n\in\textup{GAC}(\boldsymbol\mu^*,\boldsymbol\Sigma,\varepsilon)} 
        \mathbf E^{1/2}[\|\widehat{\boldsymbol\mu}_n^{\textup{IR}}-\boldsymbol\mu^*\|_2^2] 
        \le \frac{C\|\boldsymbol\Sigma\|^{1/2}_{\textup{op}}}{1 - 
        2\varepsilon - \sqrt{\varepsilon(1-\varepsilon)}}\,
        \big(\sqrt{\textbf{\textup{r}}_{\scriptscriptstyle\boldsymbol\Sigma}/n} + \varepsilon\sqrt{\log(1/
        \varepsilon)}\big),
    align
    where $\mathbf P\!_n\in\textup{GAC}(\boldsymbol\mu^*,\boldsymbol\Sigma,\varepsilon)$ means that 
    the data points $\boldsymbol X_i$ are Gaussian with adversarial contamination, 
    see 1. If, in addition, $p\ge 2$ and $n\ge p\vee 10$, then 
    align
        \sup_{\boldsymbol\mu^*\in\mathbb R^p}
        \sup_{\mathbf P\!_n\in\textup{GAC}(\boldsymbol\mu^*,\boldsymbol\Sigma,\varepsilon)} 
        \mathbf E^{1/2}[\|\widehat{\boldsymbol\mu}_n^{\textup{IR}}-\boldsymbol\mu^*\|_2^2] 
        \le \frac{10\|\boldsymbol\Sigma\|^{1/2}_{\textup{op}}}{1-2\varepsilon - \sqrt{\varepsilon(1-\varepsilon)}}\,
        \big(\sqrt{p/n} + \varepsilon\sqrt{\log(1/\varepsilon)}\big).
    align
